# Script reference

Each skill that ships a check keeps it in its own `scripts/` directory. This page quotes the header comment of
every one of them, unchanged: usage, exit codes, what it checks and what it leaves to you. The scripts are the
authority; this page is generated from them.

Copy a script into your project and run it from the repository root, as its skill's Validation section says.

## `check-bootstrap.sh`

From [`bootstrap-project`](../../skills/bootstrap-project/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/bootstrap-project/scripts/check-bootstrap.sh).

```text
scripts/check-bootstrap.sh — the mechanical half of bootstrap-project's Validation.
  usage: scripts/check-bootstrap.sh [t0|t1|t2] [--public]       run from the repository root
  The tier defaults to the one CLAUDE.md states ("Current tier: **t1**"); --public defaults to
  CLAUDE.md's "Distribution profile: Public". Tiers are cumulative: t2 runs the t0 and t1 checks too.
  exit:  0 every check passed | 1 at least one FAILED | 2 the tier could not be determined
Not checked here, because they need a person, a container runtime or a forge:
  - that the pre-commit hooks RUN successfully (run them: `lefthook run pre-commit` or
    `pre-commit run --all-files`), only that they are configured and installed;
  - that architecture/workspace.dsl validates (run the Structurizr validate for your runtime);
  - that SECURITY.md's Scope is a good threat model, only that it is filled in;
  - that private vulnerability reporting is on (GitHub: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/private-vulnerability-reporting --jq .enabled).
```

## `check-action-pins.sh`

From [`harden-github-actions`](../../skills/harden-github-actions/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/harden-github-actions/scripts/check-action-pins.sh).

```text
scripts/check-action-pins.sh
Every `uses: owner/repo@<sha> # <tag>` must pin a 40-hex commit SHA, and that SHA must be
the commit <tag> actually resolves to. A comment is a claim; this resolves it.
<tag> is resolved as a TAG (git/ref/tags/<tag>, annotated tags followed to their commit), never
through commits/<ref>, which accepts any ref: a comment that repeats the SHA, or names a branch, would
resolve to itself and pass. A comment that is a 40-hex SHA, or is not a valid tag name, fails.
  usage: scripts/check-action-pins.sh [workflow-dir]        (default .github/workflows)
Exit: 0 all pins true | 1 unpinned, unlabelled or mislabelled | 2 could not run
(2, not 0, when it cannot run or finds no `uses:` — a checker that checked nothing passed nothing.)
Needs `gh` authenticated (GH_TOKEN in CI).
```

## `check-dco.sh`

From [`harden-github-actions`](../../skills/harden-github-actions/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/harden-github-actions/scripts/check-dco.sh).

```text
scripts/check-dco.sh
DCO gate for incoming changes: every non-merge commit in BASE..HEAD must carry a
`Signed-off-by:` trailer whose email matches the commit author's.
  usage: scripts/check-dco.sh BASE [HEAD]            e.g.  check-dco.sh origin/main HEAD
Exit: 0 all signed | 1 unsigned or mismatched | 2 could not run (unresolvable range)
Contributors run none of the maintainer's hooks, so this is the enforcement point for PRs.
Merge commits are exempt: a merge certifies nothing about the merged work's authorship.
```

## `check-gitlab-pins.sh`

From [`harden-gitlab-ci`](../../skills/harden-gitlab-ci/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/harden-gitlab-ci/scripts/check-gitlab-pins.sh).

```text
scripts/check-gitlab-pins.sh — every third-party reference in a GitLab CI config is pinned.
  usage: scripts/check-gitlab-pins.sh [config]            (default .gitlab-ci.yml; run from the repo root)
  env:   GITLAB_PINS_ALLOW   ERE of image references to skip — your own registry, say
                             '^\$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE' — because they are yours to pin or not
  exit:  0 every reference is pinned | 1 at least one is not | 2 could not run
         (2, not 0, when `yq` is missing or the wrong one, a file is missing or does not parse, or the file
          mentions include:/image:/services: yet none was extracted — a checker that checked nothing passed nothing)
Checks, following `include: local` files (globs too):
  include: component   ref after the last '@' must be a 40-hex commit SHA (exact tag: WARN; ~latest, partial
                        semver, branch, a $VARIABLE or no '@': FAIL)
  include: project      `ref:` must be a 40-hex SHA (exact tag: WARN; absent — it defaults to the target's
                        HEAD — or a branch or $VARIABLE: FAIL)
  include: remote / URL no ref exists to pin: FAIL unless the URL embeds a 40-hex revision
  image: / services:    must carry @sha256:<64 hex> (anywhere in the file: global, default:, per job)
Needs mikefarah `yq` v4 (a structured read: grep cannot tell `name:` of a service from `name:` of an artifact).
```

## `check-adrs.sh`

From [`setup-adrs`](../../skills/setup-adrs/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/setup-adrs/scripts/check-adrs.sh).

```text
scripts/check-adrs.sh — the mechanical half of setup-adrs' Validation.
  usage: scripts/check-adrs.sh [adr-dir]        (default docs/adr; run from the repository root)
  exit:  0 every check passed | 1 at least one FAILED
Per ADR file: NNNN-kebab-title.md; first line "# N. Title" with N equal to the file number (the adr-tools
form Structurizr's !adrs needs); a real, not-future "Date: YYYY-MM-DD"; a "## Status" with a recognised
value; "## Context", "## Decision" and "## Consequences"; no template placeholder left in the text.
Per directory: no README.md or other non-ADR markdown; numbers unique, 0001-0003 present (gaps warn);
ADR-0003 mentions alternatives; an Operations ADR-0004 only when CLAUDE.md's Category is Infrastructure
or Hybrid (a Development project's ADR-0004 may be any decision); index.yml present and accurate for
the foundational ADRs (file exists, id, title and status agree with the ADR).
Not checked: that ADR-0002 fits the project's stack, or that ADR-0003's reasoning is sound.
```

## `check-containerfile.sh`

From [`setup-container-security`](../../skills/setup-container-security/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/setup-container-security/scripts/check-containerfile.sh).

```text
scripts/check-containerfile.sh — the mechanical half of setup-container-security.
  usage: scripts/check-containerfile.sh [file...]     default: every Containerfile*/Dockerfile* under
                                                       the repo root (3 levels deep); run from the root
  exit:  0 every check passed | 1 at least one FAILED | 2 no Containerfile found (nothing was checked)
Per file (instructions are read as logical lines, backslash continuations joined):
  FROM        every FROM names a digest (@sha256:<64 hex>); `scratch` and an earlier stage are exempt. A
              ${VARIABLE} base is expanded from its global ARG default (ARG NAME=value before the first
              FROM) and that is checked; one with no default fails, because it cannot be verified
  USER        the final stage ends on a USER that is not root or 0; an exception is declared with a
              comment line `# root-ok: <reason>` in that stage (reported, not failed)
  RUN         `curl|wget ... | sh|bash` and `sh -c "$(curl ...)"` fail; a RUN that downloads from a URL
              must verify it in the same RUN (sha256sum/sha512sum/shasum -c, gpg --verify, cosign verify),
              or sit under a comment line `# unverified-ok: <reason>`; `apt-get install` needs
              --no-install-recommends
Per repository: a .dockerignore or .containerignore (beside the file or at the root) that excludes .git
  and .env; hadolint named in lefthook.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml or a CI file; .grype.yaml present and
  grype named in a CI file; a docker ecosystem in .github/dependabot.yml when that file exists.
Not checked: that a digest is the multi-arch INDEX rather than a per-arch manifest (needs the registry:
  skopeo inspect --raw docker://IMAGE@DIGEST must say application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json), the
  scan itself, SBOM contents, HEALTHCHECK, and what an ENTRYPOINT does after start.
```

## `check-hygiene.sh`

From [`setup-git-hooks`](../../skills/setup-git-hooks/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/setup-git-hooks/scripts/check-hygiene.sh).

```text
scripts/check-hygiene.sh — the mechanical half of setup-git-hooks' Step 3 (.gitignore) and its
"Lockfile and frozen installs" rule.
  usage: scripts/check-hygiene.sh            run from the repository root
  exit:  0 every check passed | 1 at least one FAILED
.gitignore: judged by the tracked file alone in a scratch repository (your global excludes file is not
  the project's). It must ignore .env .env.local .envrc .envrc.local *.pem *.key credentials.json
  secrets.yaml CLAUDE.local.md, and must NOT ignore .env.example.
Lockfiles: for each manifest found (pyproject.toml, mix.exs, Cargo.toml, package.json) a lockfile must
  be COMMITTED — present in the index, not just on disk, and not git-ignored.
Frozen installs, in CI files (.github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml) and Containerfile*/Dockerfile*, for an
  ecosystem that has a lockfile: `uv sync` needs --frozen or --locked; `npm install` must be `npm ci`
  (npm install -g is exempt); `cargo build` needs --locked; `mix deps.get` needs --check-locked. A
  `COPY` of a lockfile through an optional glob (`mix.lock*`) is a failure: it masks a missing lockfile.
Not checked: shell scripts the CI calls, other ecosystems (Go, for one), and lines continued across
  backslashes (the command and its flag are judged on one physical line).
```

From [`validate-quality-config`](../../skills/validate-quality-config/SKILL.md). [Source](../../skills/validate-quality-config/scripts/check-tool-pins.sh).

```text
scripts/check-tool-pins.sh
Every pin of a lint/format/compliance tool must be EXACT, and every place must agree.
  usage: scripts/check-tool-pins.sh TOOL [TOOL...]     e.g.  check-tool-pins.sh reuse hadolint
Exit: 0 all pins exact and identical | 1 floating or differing pins | 2 no pin found for a tool
```
